title: Githa Hariharan v. Reserve Bank of India

content.caseIdentity: Githa Hariharan v. Reserve Bank of India, (1999) 2 SCC 228
content.facts: The Supreme Court considered a dispute concerning the interpretation of Section 6(a) of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 and the mother's position as a natural guardian.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether the expression 'after him' in Section 6(a) of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act makes the father an exclusive natural guardian during his lifetime.
content.ratioDecidendi: 'After him' in Section 6(a) does not make the mother legally incapable of being a natural guardian during the father's lifetime; the provision must be read consistently with equality and the child's welfare.
content.holding: 'After him' in Section 6(a) does not make the mother legally incapable of being a natural guardian during the father's lifetime; the provision must be read consistently with equality and the child's welfare.
content.relevance: Use this authority for the stated statutory proposition, while matching the case facts and the current statutory text before relying on it.

sources.evidenceNote: Official Supreme Court judgment confirms the case identity, judgment date and the Section 6(a) natural-guardian issue; the judgment explains that 'after him' does not render the mother incapable of acting as natural guardian during the father's lifetime.
